root_cause.text: In IPVS service editing/unbinding, `ip_vs_unbind_scheduler()` left `svc->scheduler` pointing to the old scheduler until after `done_service()` could queue RCU callbacks, creating a race where packets still selected the old scheduler while its `svc->sched_data` had already been freed after the RCU grace period.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `rcu_assign_pointer(svc->scheduler, NULL)` into `ip_vs_unbind_scheduler()` before calling `sched->done_service(svc)`, and the commit message explicitly says the old `svc->scheduler` pointer was cleared “after the scheduler module initiates RCU callbacks,” which “can cause packets to use the old scheduler at the time when svc->sched_data is already freed.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify `ip_vs_unbind_scheduler` by removing the scheduler parameter from its interface.
intent_record.what: The function prototype for `ip_vs_unbind_scheduler` was changed from taking two parameters, `struct ip_vs_service *svc` and `struct ip_vs_scheduler *sched`, to taking only one parameter, `struct ip_vs_service *svc`.
intent_record.how: At compile time, callers must now invoke `ip_vs_unbind_scheduler` with only the service object, and the scheduler argument is no longer part of the public interface. This implies the function will determine or no longer need the scheduler internally, reducing caller responsibility and preventing mismatched scheduler references.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the service cleanup code to match the new `ip_vs_unbind_scheduler()` interface.
intent_record.what: In `ip_vs_add_service()`, the call to `ip_vs_unbind_scheduler()` was changed from passing two arguments, `svc` and `sched`, to passing only `svc`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the cleanup path now uses the scheduler unbind helper with its updated single-argument interface, ensuring the service is detached from its scheduler without relying on an explicit `sched` argument in this call site.

intent_record.intent_summary: Move scheduler pointer cleanup into ip_vs_unbind_scheduler() and update the RCU wait comment accordingly.
intent_record.what: In ip_vs_edit_service(), the call to ip_vs_unbind_scheduler() was changed from passing both svc and old_sched to passing only svc, and the explicit RCU_INIT_POINTER(svc->scheduler, NULL) assignment was removed. The accompanying comment was updated from "Wait all svc->sched_data users" to "Wait all svc->scheduler/sched_data users".
intent_record.how: The unbind helper now appears to be responsible for clearing the scheduler pointer itself, so the caller no longer nulls svc->scheduler directly. Functionally, this preserves the same teardown sequence while centralizing scheduler detachment logic and ensuring RCU grace-period waiting covers users of both the scheduler pointer and associated scheduler data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restore the previous scheduler when rebinding a new scheduler fails.
intent_record.what: In the error path after a failed call to `ip_vs_bind_scheduler(svc, sched)`, the code now attempts to rebind the previous scheduler by calling `ip_vs_bind_scheduler(svc, old_sched)` if `old_sched` is non-NULL, and clears `old_sched` when that restoration succeeds.
intent_record.how: If installing the new scheduler fails, the service is now actively rolled back to its prior scheduler instead of leaving the service in a partially updated state. This preserves the original scheduling behavior and reduces the chance of the service remaining bound to the wrong scheduler after an update failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update scheduler unbinding in service deletion to use the new single-argument interface.
intent_record.what: In __ip_vs_del_service(), the call to ip_vs_unbind_scheduler() was changed from passing two arguments, (svc, old_sched), to passing only svc. The old_sched variable is still obtained with rcu_dereference_protected() and then passed to ip_vs_scheduler_put() unchanged.
intent_record.how: This changes the scheduler unbind path to use the service object alone, letting ip_vs_unbind_scheduler() obtain or manage the current scheduler internally instead of relying on the caller to pass the previously dereferenced scheduler pointer. Runtime behavior is otherwise the same in this hunk, aside from matching the revised function interface and avoiding use of the extra argument.

intent_record.intent_summary: Make scheduler unbinding clear `svc->scheduler` internally with the proper memory ordering before running cleanup callbacks.
intent_record.what: The function `ip_vs_unbind_scheduler()` changed its signature from taking `(struct ip_vs_service *svc, struct ip_vs_scheduler *sched)` to taking only `(struct ip_vs_service *svc)`. Inside the function, the local variable was renamed from `cur_sched` to `sched`, and the code now reads `svc->scheduler` with `rcu_dereference_protected()`, returns early if it is NULL, explicitly sets `svc->scheduler` to NULL with `rcu_assign_pointer()`, and adds an `smp_wmb()` before calling `sched->done_service(svc)`. The trailing comment stating that `svc->scheduler` can only be set to NULL by the caller was removed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the unbind operation now clears the service's scheduler pointer itself before invoking the scheduler's cleanup callback, instead of relying on the caller to do so. The added write memory barrier ensures that the NULLing of `svc->scheduler` is visible before any RCU-related callbacks or later schedule-path reads, reducing the chance of races where scheduling code observes an outdated scheduler pointer while unbind/cleanup is in progress.

consistency_review.core_intent: Refactor scheduler unbinding so that pointer cleanup is handled inside ip_vs_unbind_scheduler(), with callers updated to the new interface and related comments adjusted.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they move `svc->scheduler` cleanup into `ip_vs_unbind_scheduler()` and adjust the RCU timing/commentary to avoid the race where the old scheduler remains visible while its data may be freed.

The change is about restoring the previous scheduler if rebinding a new one fails, which is a failure-handling fix. It does not address the core race in `ip_vs_unbind_scheduler()` where `svc->scheduler` remained pointing to the old scheduler too long and `sched_data` could be freed before packets stopped using it.

The change is about adapting service deletion to a new single-argument scheduler unbinding interface, which is an API/signature update. It does not indicate a fix for the race where svc->scheduler remained stale and could race with RCU-freed sched_data.

The change directly matches the root cause: it ensures `svc->scheduler` is cleared with proper ordering during unbinding before cleanup/R​CU callbacks, preventing use of the old scheduler after its data may be freed.

candidates.rationale: This call site unbinds the scheduler but, in the vulnerable code, pointer cleanup was still handled separately by the caller afterward. That ordering allowed done_service() and subsequent RCU callbacks to run while svc->scheduler could still point to the old scheduler.

This unbind operation was followed by an explicit RCU_INIT_POINTER(svc->scheduler, NULL) and synchronize_rcu() in the caller, meaning the scheduler pointer remained stale until after unbind callbacks could free sched_data.

This caller-side cleanup happened after ip_vs_unbind_scheduler() returned, so during the window around done_service() and RCU callback scheduling, svc->scheduler could still reference the old scheduler, enabling the race described.

The done_service callback is the cleanup hook that can trigger freeing of scheduler-specific data; if svc->scheduler is not cleared before this runs, packet processing may still select the old scheduler while its sched_data is being torn down.

This callback executes the scheduler teardown while the comment explicitly says svc->scheduler can only be cleared by the caller, which is the core bug: the stale scheduler pointer remains valid during cleanup and can race with packet selection.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unbind call occurred before the caller cleared svc->scheduler, leaving the old scheduler reachable while done_service() and later RCU callbacks could free scheduler-specific data, matching the stale-pointer race in the root cause.
Clearing svc->scheduler only here, after unbind cleanup had already run, created the window where packets could still select the old scheduler while its sched_data was being torn down.

This callback performs scheduler teardown while svc->scheduler was still expected to be cleared by the caller, enabling the race where cleanup and RCU freeing happened before the pointer was invalidated.
